name: Candle
citation: BIPM (2019) The International System of Units (SI Brochure), 9th edition
notes: The candela grew out of the candle; a candle is about 1 cd

name: LED light bulb (60-100 W equivalent)
citation: U.S. Department of Energy, Lumens and the Lighting Facts label

name: Sun
citation: Littlefair P.J. (1985) The luminous efficacy of daylight: a review. Lighting Res Technol 17, 162
notes: Computed: 3.828e26 W x about 93 lm/W / 4 pi

name: Car main-beam headlamps (legal maximum)
citation: UNECE Regulation No 48: installation of lighting and light-signalling devices, para 6.1.9.1 (aggregate main beam at most 430000 cd)
notes: All main beams together may not exceed 430000 cd

name: Full Moon (as seen from Earth)
citation: Kyba C.C.M., Mohar A. & Posch T. (2017) How bright is moonlight? Astronomy & Geophysics 58, 1.31
notes: Computed: 0.05-0.32 lx at the ground times the distance squared

name: Sirius A
citation: van Leeuwen F. (2007) Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction. A&A 474, 653
notes: Computed from V = -1.46 at 2.64 pc (M_V = 1.43) and the Sun's M_V = 4.81 (Willmer 2018)

name: Type Ia supernova at peak
citation: Phillips M.M. (1993) The absolute magnitudes of Type Ia supernovae. ApJ 413, L105
notes: Computed from peak M_V about -19.3: one star outshines a galaxy for weeks

name: Quasar 3C 273
citation: Schmidt M. (1963) 3C 273: a star-like object with large red-shift. Nature 197, 1040
notes: Computed from V = 12.9 at z = 0.158 (luminosity distance about 750 Mpc): M_V about -26.5

name: Gamma-ray burst GRB 080319B (optical peak)
citation: Bloom J.S. et al. (2009) Observations of the naked-eye GRB 080319B: implications of nature's brightest explosion. ApJ 691, 723
notes: Peak visual magnitude 5.3 from 6 Gpc: M about -38.6 (computed): the brightest optical event ever recorded
